- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment is uniformly neutral or negative (0.00) and price is trending upward, model underestimates upside; add 2–5% bias to forecast for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.67) after a downtrend, model often lags; shift forecast upward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% in final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is falling, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid premature bottoming.
